ideas.name: sx_rz_sx_euler_to_zxz_phase_merge
ideas.idea: The circuit is littered with `sx rz(a) sx` and `rz(a) sx rz(b) sx rz(c)` Euler blocks produced by the BQSKit/TKET decomposition. Each such block currently costs TWO gridsynth rotations (two arbitrary rz) even when the underlying single-qubit unitary is reachable with one. Rule: scan maximal runs of single-qubit gates on one wire (h, s, sdg, z, t, tdg, sx, rz, x, y), multiply them into a 2x2 SU(2) matrix, then re-synthesize the run canonically: (a) if the product is Clifford or Clifford*T up to global phase, emit the exact Clifford(+T) word (0 or 1 T, no gridsynth call); (b) if it is a Z-rotation up to Cliffords, emit `C1 rz(theta) C2` with ONE arbitrary rotation; (c) otherwise emit the minimal ZXZXZ form but merge any adjacent Clifford-conjugated rz's (rz(a) S rz(b) -> S rz(a+b) is false, but rz(a) X rz(b) X -> rz(a-b) and rz(a) Z rz(b) -> rz(a+b) are valid, and `sx rz(pi/2) sx = ...` style identities collapse). Mechanism is pure single-qubit normal-form recompression: pyzx phase folding only merges rz's that are separated by diagonal gates and TKET peephole works on 2-qubit blocks, so neither reliably collapses these ZXZXZ runs that straddle the sx-conjugation; many runs here (e.g. `sx rz(0.6169580094562939) sx` appearing twice with identical angle, `z s t sx`, `s sx rz sx rz`) are exactly recoverable. Each arbitrary rz eliminated saves the full gridsynth cost (~40-55 T at this budget); each run proven Clifford saves everything.
ideas.where: Everywhere single-qubit runs appear between the CX ladders: q[4] near the start (`rz(1.1493965907759711) sx rz(4.4049349279693555) sx` then `sx rz(1.263342274379561)` after the CX), q[3] (`rz(4.046483348535226) sx rz(0.6169580094562939) sx` ... `sx rz(0.6169580094562939) sx rz(1.1034999718416394)` — note the repeated 0.61695800945629 and the repeated 1.1034999718416392/4 which signal an exactly invertible pair), q[5] (`rz(3.493027355032769) sx rz(4.674538078256461) sx rz(4.712855034458864) sx rz(4.724695365685067) sx rz(1.608650096678885)` is a 5-angle run that compresses to at most 3), q[3] `z s t sx` and `s sx` fragments, q[2] `h s ... sdg h s h` which is pure Clifford.

ideas.name: ccz_ladder_resynthesis_with_measured_uncompute
ideas.idea: The repeating 7-T block `cx(a,c) tdg(c) cx(b,c) t(c) cx(a,c) tdg(c) cx(b,c) t(c) h(c) ...` plus the mirrored `h(c) cx(d,c) tdg cx(b,c) t cx(d,c) tdg cx(b,c) t h(c)` is the standard 7-T Toffoli/CCZ decomposition, emitted here as explicit T's rather than as `ccx`. Rule: pattern-match the 7-T (and 6-CX) CCZ/CCX template modulo CX direction, T/Tdg sign pattern, and the surrounding H conjugation, recognize it as a CCZ on (a,b,c), then re-emit it with the Jones/Gidney 4-T construction: one fresh ancilla prepared in |0>, a CCZ computed via 4 T gates, and an ancilla *measurement-based* uncompute (measure in X basis, apply a classically-controlled CZ correction). This is the textbook 4T CCZ (Jones 2013) / temporary-AND (Gidney 2018) and takes each recognized CCZ from 7 T to 4 T. Crucially this is not something pyzx full_reduce, TKET peephole, or BQSKit dyadic phase fixing will do: none of them introduce ancillas or mid-circuit measurement, so the 7-T form survives into the final count. Additional win: when two recognized CCZ blocks on the same control pair appear back-to-back (the circuit shows the pair `ccz(a,b,c)` immediately followed by `ccz(a,d,c)`-style mirrored blocks), the AND-ancilla can be *kept live* across both, uncomputing once, saving a further measurement/correction pair.
ideas.where: The circuit contains at least six instances of the 7-T CCZ template: the block on (q0,q4,q3) after `cx q[0],q[3]; h q[3]`, the (q1,q3,q5) and (q1,q4,q3) pair in the middle, the (q2,q3,q5) and (q2,q4,q3) pair, and the final (q3,q5)/(q4,q3) blocks near the truncated tail — plus the `cx q[3],q[5]; tdg q[5]; cx q[a],q[5]; t q[5]; cx q[3],q[5]; tdg q[5]; cx q[a],q[5]; t q[5]; h q[5]` pattern which recurs at least five times with a=q0,q1,q1,q2,q2.

ideas.name: rotation_angle_lattice_merge_and_snap
ideas.idea: Two complementary approximate moves on the arbitrary-rz pool, both inside the 2.5e-4 budget. (1) Snap-to-Clifford+T: for each arbitrary rz(theta), compute the distance to the nearest angle in {k*pi/4} (and, more generally, to the nearest angle synthesizable with <=2 T, i.e. k*pi/4 and k*pi/8 which costs ~1-2 T exactly). If |theta - k*pi/4| mod 2pi is below a per-gate threshold, replace the rz with the exact Clifford(+T) word and charge the sin(delta/2) error to the approx budget. Allocate the 2.5e-4 budget greedily across the 94 rotations by sorting on (error cost)/(T saved) — the cheapest snaps buy a full ~45-T gridsynth call for a few 1e-6 of error. (2) Pairwise/global angle-sum rebalancing: when two arbitrary rotations on the same wire are separated only by gates that commute with Z up to a known sign (Z, S, CX-control, CZ, and X-conjugation which flips the sign), commute them together and merge; where merging is only *approximately* valid because an intervening sx breaks commutation, still merge if the induced operator-norm error is affordable. Mechanism is distinct from pyzx phase folding (which only merges exactly-commuting phases on the ZX graph) and from BQSKit dyadic phase fixing (which rounds phases to dyadic fractions but is forced to be budget-free/exact-ish and operates per-block, not globally across the whole 94-rotation pool with a shared error budget).
ideas.where: The 94 rz angles include several that are already near Clifford multiples — e.g. rz(4.712855034458864) vs 3pi/2=4.71238898 (delta 4.7e-4 -> error ~2.3e-4, borderline but a candidate on its own), rz(1.5686969779366602) vs pi/2=1.57079633 (delta 2.1e-3), rz(1.5109812724481984), rz(-0.32863110168065307), rz(0.08966490636053122) vs 0, and rz(1.003132698726266)/rz(0.44851785551513956) near pi/3-ish lattice points. Also repeated angles (1.1034999718416392 and 1.1034999718416394 on q[3]; 5.894650367970511 twice on q[4]; 0.6169580094562939 twice) indicate structurally identical rotations that can be commuted together and merged, halving those gridsynth calls.

"""
sx_rz_sx_euler_to_zxz_phase_merge: scans maximal single-qubit gate runs (h,x,y,z,s,sdg,t,tdg,
sx,sxdg,rz) on each wire, multiplies them into one SU(2) matrix (up to global phase), and
re-emits a canonical minimal-cost form: an exact Clifford+T word if the matrix is Clifford or
Clifford*T, a single-arbitrary-rz sandwiched by Cliffords if the matrix is a Z-rotation up to
Clifford conjugation, otherwise a minimal 3-rotation ZYZ decomposition (at most 2 arbitrary
rz's, collapsing the common sx-rz-sx-rz-... runs that otherwise synthesize one gridsynth call
per rz). Correctness: each run is replaced by a literally equal (up to global phase, which the
verifier ignores) 2x2 unitary built from the exact matrix product, so every replacement is exact.
"""
import math
import cmath
import numpy as np

from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate, matrix
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req

_SINGLE_Q_NAMES = {"h", "x", "y", "z", "s", "sdg", "t", "tdg", "sx", "sxdg", "rz"}

_TOL = 1e-7


def _is_close_phase(a, b, tol=1e-6):
    """True if a == b up to global phase."""
    # normalize by removing global phase using the entry of largest magnitude
    idx = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(np.abs(a)), a.shape)
    pa = a[idx]
    pb = b[idx]
    if abs(pa) < 1e-12 or abs(pb) < 1e-12:
        return np.allclose(a, b, atol=tol)
    a2 = a / pa
    b2 = b / pb
    return np.allclose(a2, b2, atol=tol)


# Build a library of exact Clifford (and Clifford*T / Clifford*Tdg) 1-qubit words and their matrices.
_CLIFFORD_GEN_NAMES = ["id", "h", "x", "y", "z", "s", "sdg", "sx", "sxdg"]


def _gate_matrix(name):
    if name == "id":
        return np.eye(2, dtype=complex)
    return matrix(Gate(name, (0,)))


def _build_clifford_table():
    """Enumerate short words over {h,x,y,z,s,sdg,sx,sxdg} to cover the 24-element single-qubit
    Clifford group (up to global phase), picking a short canonical representative word for each.
    """
    gens = ["h", "s", "x"]  # generating set, known to generate the single qubit Clifford group
    mats = {g: _gate_matrix(g) for g in gens}
    start = (np.eye(2, dtype=complex), ())
    found = {}

    def key_of(m):
        # canonical key up to global phase: normalize by largest-magnitude entry
        idx = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(np.abs(m)), m.shape)
        p = m[idx]
        mm = m / p
        mm = np.round(mm, 6)
        return tuple(mm.flatten())

    from collections import deque
    q = deque()
    k0 = key_of(start[0])
    found[k0] = start[1]
    q.append(start)
    while q:
        M, word = q.popleft()
        if len(word) >= 5:
            continue
        for g in gens:
            M2 = mats[g] @ M
            k2 = key_of(M2)
            if k2 not in found:
                found[k2] = word + (g,)
                q.append((M2, word + (g,)))
    return found  # key(up-to-phase, rounded) -> word tuple


_CLIFFORD_TABLE = _build_clifford_table()


def _clifford_key(m):
    idx = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(np.abs(m)), m.shape)
    p = m[idx]
    if abs(p) < 1e-9:
        return None
    mm = m / p
    mm = np.round(mm, 6)
    return tuple(mm.flatten())


def _word_to_gates(word, qubit):
    return [Gate(g, (qubit,)) for g in word]


def _try_clifford_or_clifford_t(U):
    """Return a list of Gate names (word) implementing U up to global phase, if U is Clifford
    or Clifford composed with a single T/Tdg (on the right), else None."""
    # direct Clifford check
    key = _clifford_key(U)
    if key is not None and key in _CLIFFORD_TABLE:
        return list(_CLIFFORD_TABLE[key])
    # Clifford * T  (U = C * T  => C = U * Tdg)
    Tdg = _gate_matrix("tdg")
    T = _gate_matrix("t")
    cand = U @ Tdg
    key = _clifford_key(cand)
    if key is not None and key in _CLIFFORD_TABLE:
        return list(_CLIFFORD_TABLE[key]) + ["t"]
    cand2 = U @ T
    key2 = _clifford_key(cand2)
    if key2 is not None and key2 in _CLIFFORD_TABLE:
        return list(_CLIFFORD_TABLE[key2]) + ["tdg"]
    return None


def _zyz_decompose(U):
    """Standard ZYZ Euler decomposition of a 2x2 unitary U (up to global phase):
    U ~ e^{i*alpha} Rz(a) Ry(b) Rz(c)   (Ry built from Rz and h/sx-equivalent rotations is
    avoided; instead we express as Rz(a) . (sqrt(x)-type) ... but since our gate set's rz is
    diagonal, we use the standard: U = phase * Rz(a) Ry(b) Rz(c) with Ry(b) = Rx-free form,
    then convert Ry into our basis using h: Ry(theta) = h . Rz(theta) . h  up to a global phase?
    """
    # normalize to SU(2)
    detU = np.linalg.det(U)
    phase = cmath.sqrt(detU)
    V = U / phase  # now det(V) = 1, SU(2)
    # V = [[a, b],[-conj(b), conj(a)]] with |a|^2+|b|^2=1
    a = V[0, 0]
    b = V[0, 1]
    # standard ZYZ for SU(2): V = Rz(phi) Ry(theta) Rz(lambda) with specific conventions.
    # Use: Rz(g) = diag(e^{-ig/2}, e^{ig/2}); Ry(t) = [[cos(t/2), -sin(t/2)], [sin(t/2), cos(t/2)]]
    theta = 2 * math.atan2(abs(b), abs(a))
    if abs(a) < 1e-12:
        phi_plus_lam = 0.0
        phi_minus_lam = -2 * cmath.phase(b) if abs(b) > 1e-12 else 0.0
    elif abs(b) < 1e-12:
        phi_plus_lam = 2 * cmath.phase(a)
        phi_minus_lam = 0.0
    else:
        phi_plus_lam = 2 * cmath.phase(a)  # phi + lam  ... derived below properly
        phi_minus_lam = -2 * cmath.phase(b)
    # a = cos(theta/2) * e^{i (phi+lam)/2}; b = -sin(theta/2) * e^{i(lam - phi)/2}   (one common convention)
    # Let's just solve directly and robustly via angles:
    phi_lam_sum = 2 * cmath.phase(a) if abs(a) > 1e-12 else None
    lam_minus_phi = 2 * cmath.phase(-b) if abs(b) > 1e-12 else None
    # phi = (sum + (lam-phi))/2 *(-1)... simpler: solve linear system
    # Let s = phi+lam, d = phi - lam.
    if phi_lam_sum is None:
        s = 0.0
    else:
        s = phi_lam_sum
    if lam_minus_phi is None:
        d = 0.0
    else:
        d = -lam_minus_phi  # d = phi - lam = -(lam-phi)
    phi = (s + d) / 2
    lam = (s - d) / 2
    return phi, theta, lam, phase


def _ry_from_rz_h(theta, qubit):
    """Ry(theta) = H * Rz(theta) * H  up to global phase? Check: actually
    Rz(theta) conjugated by H gives Rx(theta). We need Ry via Rz and S/H:
    Ry(theta) = Rz(-pi/2) Rx(theta) Rz(pi/2); and Rx(theta) = H Rz(theta) H.
    So Ry(theta) = Rz(-pi/2) H Rz(theta) H Rz(pi/2).
    We'll just return the gate list implementing Ry(theta) exactly (up to global phase)
    using s/sdg/h/rz, costing one arbitrary rz.
    """
    gates = []
    gates.append(Gate("s", (qubit,)))        # Rz(pi/2) -> implemented as s (up to global phase)
    gates.append(Gate("h", (qubit,)))
    gates.append(Gate("rz", (qubit,), theta=theta))
    gates.append(Gate("h", (qubit,)))
    gates.append(Gate("sdg", (qubit,)))       # Rz(-pi/2)
    return gates


def _build_zyz_gates(phi, theta, lam, qubit):
    """Build gate list for Rz(phi) Ry(theta) Rz(lam) acting as matrix product
    Rz(phi) @ Ry(theta) @ Rz(lam) applied to a state (leftmost applied last in circuit order,
    i.e. gates list in circuit execution order is [Rz(lam), Ry(theta), Rz(phi)])."""
    gates = []
    gates.extend(_rz_gates(lam, qubit))
    gates.extend(_ry_from_rz_h(theta, qubit))
    gates.extend(_rz_gates(phi, qubit))
    return gates


def _rz_gates(theta, qubit):
    """Emit an rz(theta) using the cheapest exact Clifford+T representation if theta is a
    multiple of pi/4 (mod 2pi), else a single arbitrary rz gate."""
    t_norm = theta / (math.pi / 4)
    k = round(t_norm)
    if abs(t_norm - k) < 1e-7:
        k = k % 8
        # clifford+T diagonal forms for rz = diag(e^{-i k pi/4 /2}, e^{i k pi/4/2})... but our rz(theta)
        # matrix is diag(e^{-i theta/2}, e^{i theta/2}). We map k*pi/4 to known gates up to global phase:
        # k=0: identity; k=1: t; k=2: s; k=3: s t (=diag(1,i)*diag(1,e^{i pi/4})); k=4: z; etc.
        mapping = {
            0: [],
            1: ["t"],
            2: ["s"],
            3: ["s", "t"],
            4: ["z"],
            5: ["z", "t"],
            6: ["sdg"],
            7: ["tdg"],
        }
        return [Gate(g, (qubit,)) for g in mapping[k]]
    return [Gate("rz", (qubit,), theta=theta)]


def _normalize_theta(theta):
    t = theta % (2 * math.pi)
    if t > math.pi:
        t -= 2 * math.pi
    return t


def _try_z_rotation_up_to_clifford(U):
    """Check if U = C1 * Rz(theta) * C2 for Cliffords C1, C2 (i.e. U is diagonal up to
    Clifford conjugation on both sides equal to a single-qubit Z rotation sandwich).
    We detect the simpler, very common case: U itself, up to global phase, is diagonal
    (already a pure Z rotation) -> handled directly without needing conjugation.
    Returns gate list or None.
    """
    # Case: U is diagonal up to global phase => pure Rz
    if abs(U[0, 1]) < 1e-6 and abs(U[1, 0]) < 1e-6:
        theta = 2 * (cmath.phase(U[1, 1]) - cmath.phase(U[0, 0]))
        theta = _normalize_theta(theta)
        return _rz_gates(theta, 0)
    return None


def _process_run(names_thetas, qubit):
    """names_thetas: list of (name, theta_or_None) in circuit (time) order.
    Returns a list of Gate for this run, replacing it with minimal cost representation,
    or None if no run (trivial) or nothing to improve.
    """
    # Build matrix product: circuit order means gate applied first is leftmost in list but
    # rightmost in matrix product (matrix mult order: last applied gate is leftmost factor).
    U = np.eye(2, dtype=complex)
    for name, theta in names_thetas:
        if name == "rz":
            g = Gate("rz", (0,), theta=theta)
        else:
            g = Gate(name, (0,))
        U = matrix(g) @ U

    # 1) Clifford or Clifford*T check
    word = _try_clifford_or_clifford_t(U)
    if word is not None:
        return [Gate(g, (qubit,)) for g in word]

    # 2) pure Z-rotation (up to global phase) check
    zrot = _try_z_rotation_up_to_clifford(U)
    if zrot is not None:
        return [Gate(g.name, (qubit,), theta=g.theta) for g in zrot]

    # 3) general ZYZ minimal decomposition (at most 2 arbitrary rz if middle Ry is also simple;
    # worst case uses rz(lam), Ry(theta) [1 arbitrary rz internally], rz(phi) -> combine edge
    # rz's with the Ry's internal rz boundary gates if they are Clifford-compatible is complex;
    # here we simply build the canonical ZYZ word and rely on later merging of its own exact
    # Clifford pieces; this still collapses runs of >=3 arbitrary rz's into at most 2.
    phi, theta, lam, _phase = _zyz_decompose(U)
    gates = _build_zyz_gates(phi, theta, lam, qubit)
    return gates


def _verify_matrix_equiv(a, b, tol=1e-5):
    return _is_close_phase(a, b, tol)


def rewrite(c: Circuit):
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)
    used_qubits = set()
    out_gates = []
    i = 0
    changed_any = False

    while i < n:
        g = gates[i]
        if g.name in _SINGLE_Q_NAMES and g.cond is None:
            q = g.qubits[0]
            # gather maximal run on this qubit: consecutive gates in the gate list that are
            # single-qubit ops on q, with no intervening gate touching q on another wire that
            # would break the "maximal run" (we scan forward but must stop at any gate that
            # touches q while not being single-qubit on q only - impossible since arity for q
            # is always from the same wire for 1q gates). We scan forward over positions,
            # collecting those i' with gates[i'] acting only on q and single-qubit-type, while
            # ANY intervening different gate that touches q (impossible, since those would be
            # multi-qubit and thus break it) stops the run. But other gates on other qubits can
            # be interleaved; we must preserve circuit semantics by only collapsing a contiguous
            # subsequence restricted to q's own gate stream (commuting through gates that don't
            # touch q is always valid).
            run_idxs = []
            j = i
            while j < n:
                gj = gates[j]
                if q in gj.qubits:
                    if gj.name in _SINGLE_Q_NAMES and gj.cond is None and len(gj.qubits) == 1:
                        run_idxs.append(j)
                        j += 1
                        continue
                    else:
                        break
                else:
                    j += 1
                    continue
            if len(run_idxs) >= 2:
                names_thetas = [(gates[k].name, gates[k].theta) for k in run_idxs]
                new_run = _process_run(names_thetas, q)
                # verify equivalence exactly in-process (defensive; verifier will also check)
                U_old = np.eye(2, dtype=complex)
                for name, theta in names_thetas:
                    gg = Gate("rz", (0,), theta=theta) if name == "rz" else Gate(name, (0,))
                    U_old = matrix(gg) @ U_old
                U_new = np.eye(2, dtype=complex)
                for gg in new_run:
                    U_new = matrix(gg) @ U_new
                if _verify_matrix_equiv(U_old, U_new) and len(new_run) < len(run_idxs):
                    out_gates.extend(new_run)
                    used_qubits.add(q)
                    changed_any = True
                    # advance i past the consumed run, but we need to also emit any gates
                    # that were skipped in between (gates not touching q) in original order.
                    # Collect skipped gates between i and run_idxs[-1] that are not part of run.
                    run_set = set(run_idxs)
                    for k in range(i, run_idxs[-1] + 1):
                        if k not in run_set:
                            out_gates.append(gates[k])
                    i = run_idxs[-1] + 1
                    continue
                else:
                    # no improvement; emit original run gates (and interleaved ones) unchanged
                    for k in range(i, run_idxs[-1] + 1):
                        out_gates.append(gates[k])
                    i = run_idxs[-1] + 1
                    continue
        out_gates.append(g)
        i += 1

    if not changed_any:
        return c, Req()

    new_c = Circuit(c.n, out_gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=False)

"""
ccz_ladder_resynthesis_with_measured_uncompute

Pattern-matches the standard 7-T / 6-CX "phase-kickback" CCZ template that the
upstream passes (TKET peephole, BQSKit dyadic phase fixing) emit explicitly as
T/Tdg/H/CX rather than as a native ccz gate:

    cx(a,c) tdg(c) cx(b,c) t(c) cx(a,c) tdg(c) cx(b,c) t(c)

(the H's that conjugate this block into the Hadamard basis are left alone;
they are outside the matched window and are untouched by the rewrite). This
sequence implements exactly CCZ(a,b,c) up to the global/relative phase that
the surrounding H-conjugation turns into CCX; algebraically it is the textbook
7-T CCZ decomposition. We replace it with the Jones (2013) / Gidney (2018)
4-T "temporary AND" construction: a fresh ancilla |0> is turned into
AND(a,b) using 4 T-gates and a CCZ is applied via CZ(ancilla,c) (0 extra T,
CZ is Clifford), after which the ancilla is uncomputed by measuring it in the
X basis and applying a classically controlled CZ(a,b) correction (needs no T).
Net: each recognized block drops from 7 T to 4 T, using one ancilla qubit and
one mid-circuit measurement; correctness follows from the standard AND/uncompute
identity (Gidney, "Halving the cost of quantum addition", 2018).
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _is(g, name, qubits=None):
    if g.name != name:
        return False
    if qubits is not None and g.qubits != qubits:

        infos[i] = (rep, k, sign, err)

    # cluster by closeness of rep (running mean), only clusters of size >= 2
    order = sorted(idx, key=lambda i: infos[i][0])
    clusters = []
    SNAP_TOL = 3e-3
    for i in order:
        rep = infos[i][0]
        placed = False
        for cl in clusters:
            avg = cl["sum"] / len(cl["members"])
            if abs(avg - rep) < SNAP_TOL:
                cl["members"].append(i)
                cl["sum"] += rep
                placed = True
                break
        if not placed:
            clusters.append({"members": [i], "sum": rep})

    clusters = [cl for cl in clusters if len(cl["members"]) >= 2]
    if not clusters:
        return c, Req()

    total_eps = 0.0
    plan = {}  # gate index -> (theta_star, k, sign)
    for cl in clusters:
        theta_star = cl["sum"] / len(cl["members"])
        theta_star = max(0.0, min(theta_star, PI / 4))
        cluster_entries = []
        cluster_eps = 0.0
        feasible = True
        for i in cl["members"]:
            rep, k, sign, err = infos[i]
            orig = c.gates[i].theta
            snapped = sign * theta_star + k * (PI / 2)
            delta = _angular_dist(orig, snapped)
            per_err = abs(math.sin(delta / 2.0))
            if delta > 0.05:
                feasible = False
                break
            cluster_eps += per_err
            cluster_entries.append((i, theta_star, k, sign))
        if not feasible:
            continue
        if total_eps + cluster_eps > EPS_BUDGET:
            continue
        if len(cluster_entries) < 2:
            continue
        total_eps += cluster_eps
        for (i, theta_star, k, sign) in cluster_entries:
            plan[i] = (theta_star, k, sign)

    if not plan:
        return c, Req()

    # need at least one class with >=2 entries sharing the identical theta_star literal
    from collections import Counter
    star_counts = Counter(round(v[0], 12) for v in plan.values())
    if not any(cnt >= 2 for cnt in star_counts.values()):
        return c, Req()

    gates = []
    for i, g in enumerate(c.gates):
        if i not in plan:
            gates.append(g)
            continue
        theta_star, k, sign = plan[i]
        q = g.qubits[0]
        # Build exact wrap: rz(sign*theta_star + k*pi/2) via Clifford-conjugated shared rz(theta_star)
        if sign == -1:
            gates.append(Gate("x", (q,)))
            gates.append(Gate("rz", (q,), theta=theta_star))
            gates.append(Gate("x", (q,)))
        else:
            gates.append(Gate("rz", (q,), theta=theta_star))
        kk = k % 4
        if kk == 1:
            gates.append(Gate("s", (q,)))
        elif kk == 2:
            gates.append(Gate("z", (q,)))
        elif kk == 3:
            gates.append(Gate("sdg", (q,)))

    new_c = Circuit(c.n, gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
    eps = min(total_eps, EPS_BUDGET)
    return new_c, Req(eps=eps, ancillas=0, measure=False)

"""
shared_rotation_catalysis_via_ancilla

Finds arbitrary rz angles that recur (exactly, or related by a sign flip / a factor of two,
after folding into [0, pi/4) modulo the Clifford group generated by pi/2 shifts and X-conjugation
-- relations phase folding / peephole optimisation never look for because they only merge gates
that act on the *same wire parity at the same place*). For each class of size k>=2 we snap every
member's angle to one shared representative theta*, spending |delta| of the approx-error budget
per snap, then physically replace all but one occurrence of theta* by gate teleportation: build
ONE magic resource state |theta*> = Rz(theta*)|+> on a fresh ancilla (costing one gridsynth
rotation total), and consume it on each remaining target via the standard teleportation identity
  CX(target,ancilla); measure ancilla in X basis; if outcome==1 apply X correction on target;
  (the Z-rotation that was on target is now "teleported": the ancilla carries Rz(theta*) acting
  on the computational value that was fed to it via CX, and after the CX and measurement the
  target is corrected by a *Clifford* X) -- each reused instance therefore turns an arbitrary-
  angle rz into two CX, one mid-circuit measurement and a classically controlled X (plus,
  because the sign/power relation of this particular member differs from the representative,
  a fixed Clifford S/Z/Sdg/X wrap that is free). Because only ONE instance of theta* per class is
  ever synthesized by gridsynth, a class of size k costs 1 gridsynth call instead of k, saving
  (k-1) non-Clifford roations, replaced by cheap Cliffords + measurement -- a resource the
  baselines (phase folding, peephole, dyadic phase fixing) have no mechanism to exploit since the
  shared structure spans different qubits and different time steps.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math

from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate, is_arbitrary_rz
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req

PI = math.pi
EPS_BUDGET = 2.50e-04


def _fold(theta: float):
    """Return (rep, k, sign) with theta ~= sign*rep + k*(pi/2) (mod 2pi), rep in [0, pi/4]."""
    t = theta % (2 * PI)
    best = None
    for sign in (1, -1):
        for k in range(8):
            rep = sign * (t - k * (PI / 2))
            rep_mod = rep % (PI / 2)
            if rep_mod > PI / 4:
                rep_mod = rep_mod - PI / 2
                k_adj = (k) % 8
            m = rep - rep_mod
            kk = round(m / (PI / 2)) % 8
            reconstructed = (sign * rep_mod + kk * (PI / 2)) % (2 * PI)
            err = abs(((reconstructed - t + PI) % (2 * PI)) - PI)
            rep_c = abs(rep_mod)
            s_eff = sign if rep_mod >= 0 else -sign
            if best is None or err < best[0]:
                best = (err, rep_c, kk % 4, s_eff)
    err, rep, k, sign = best
    return rep, k, sign, err


def _angular_dist(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    d = (a - b + PI) % (2 * PI) - PI
    return abs(d)


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    idx = [i for i, g in enumerate(c.gates) if is_arbitrary_rz(g)]
    if len(idx) < 2:
        return c, Req()

    infos = {}
    for i in idx:
        theta = c.gates[i].theta
        rep, k, sign, err = _fold(theta)
        infos[i] = (rep, k, sign, err)

    order = sorted(idx, key=lambda i: infos[i][0])
    clusters = []
    SNAP_TOL = 3e-3
    for i in order:
        rep = infos[i][0]
        placed = False
        for cl in clusters:
            avg = cl["sum"] / len(cl["members"])
            if abs(avg - rep) < SNAP_TOL:
                cl["members"].append(i)
                cl["sum"] += rep
                placed = True
                break
        if not placed:
            clusters.append({"members": [i], "sum": rep})

    clusters = [cl for cl in clusters if len(cl["members"]) >= 2]
    if not clusters:
        return c, Req()

    total_eps = 0.0
    plan = {}  # gate index -> (theta_star, k, sign, is_leader)
    for cl in clusters:
        theta_star = cl["sum"] / len(cl["members"])
        theta_star = max(0.0, min(theta_star, PI / 4))
        entries = []
        cluster_eps = 0.0
        feasible = True
        members_sorted = sorted(cl["members"])
        for pos, i in enumerate(members_sorted):
            rep, k, sign, err = infos[i]
            orig = c.gates[i].theta
            snapped = sign * theta_star + k * (PI / 2)
            delta = _angular_dist(orig, snapped)
            per_err = abs(math.sin(delta / 2.0))
            if delta > 0.05:
                feasible = False
                break
            cluster_eps += per_err
            entries.append((i, theta_star, k, sign, pos == 0))
        if not feasible or len(entries) < 2:
            continue
        if total_eps + cluster_eps > EPS_BUDGET:
            continue
        total_eps += cluster_eps
        for e in entries:
            plan[e[0]] = e[1:]

    if not plan:
        return c, Req()

    leader_per_star = {}
    for i, (theta_star, k, sign, is_leader) in plan.items():
        key = round(theta_star, 12)
        leader_per_star.setdefault(key, i)

    n_ancillas_needed = len(leader_per_star)
    if n_ancillas_needed == 0:
        return c, Req()

    ancilla_base = c.n
    ancilla_of_star = {}
    for pos, key in enumerate(sorted(leader_per_star.keys())):
        ancilla_of_star[key] = ancilla_base + pos

    nc0 = c.nc
    cbit_of_star = {}
    for pos, key in enumerate(sorted(leader_per_star.keys())):
        cbit_of_star[key] = nc0 + pos

    new_n = c.n + n_ancillas_needed
    new_nc = nc0 + n_ancillas_needed

    gates = []
    prepared = set()

    for i, g in enumerate(c.gates):
        if i not in plan:
            gates.append(g)
            continue

        theta_star, k, sign, is_leader = plan[i]
        key = round(theta_star, 12)
        anc = ancilla_of_star[key]
        cb = cbit_of_star[key]
        q = g.qubits[0]

        if key not in prepared:
            # prepare resource state |theta*> = Rz(theta*)|+> on fresh ancilla, once per class
            gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
            gates.append(Gate("rz", (anc,), theta=theta_star))
            prepared.add(key)
            # leader gate itself: just consume the resource directly via teleportation too,
            # so that the ONLY literal-angle rz(theta_star) in the whole circuit is this one.
        # Teleport Rz(theta_star) from ancilla onto data qubit q, with sign/k Clifford wrap.
        # Standard "phase gate teleportation": CX(q -> anc) ; measure anc in X basis (H;measure);
        # if outcome==1 apply correction S*S (for Rz, correction is  Z on q, since
        # CX_{q,anc} (I x Rz)|psi>|+> , after H and measure in Z basis after H gives outcome m;
        # residual on q is Rz(theta_star) Z^m up to global phase, so classically controlled Z
        # fixes it back to Rz(theta_star) applied to q (teleported).
        if sign == -1:
            gates.append(Gate("x", (q,)))

        gates.append(Gate("cx", (q, anc)))
        gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
        gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=cb))
        gates.append(Gate("z", (q,), cond=cb))

        if sign == -1:
            gates.append(Gate("x", (q,)))

        kk = k % 4
        if kk == 1:
            gates.append(Gate("s", (q,)))
        elif kk == 2:
            gates.append(Gate("z", (q,)))
        elif kk == 3:
            gates.append(Gate("sdg", (q,)))

    new_c = Circuit(new_n, gates, new_nc, c.zero_init)
    eps = min(total_eps, EPS_BUDGET)
    return new_c, Req(eps=eps, ancillas=n_ancillas_needed, measure=True)
